newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORDIC SKIING-VIALBE WINS ONE GOLD TOO MANY.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-VIALBE WINS ONE GOLD TOO MANY.

text.p: No woman had ever won five gold medals at one Nordic skiing world championships but that is one record that Yelena Vialbe would have been happier not to set.
Russian Vialbe, who had already triumphed in the 15-km, the 10-km pursuit and the relay, crowned a brilliant performance by winning Saturday's 30-km race.

But she could have done without the gold in last Sunday's 5-km classic, which was awarded to her after compatriot Lyubov Yegorova was stripped of her world title for testing positive for a banned stimulant.
That medal allowed Vialbe to become the first woman to make a clean sweep in all races since five events were first introduced at the world championships in 1989.
Galina Kulakova of the Soviet Union previously won all races in one championships in 1974, but only three events were held.

The 28-year-old Vialbe, who had established herself as the most successful woman in cross-country skiing even before coming to Trondheim, had already earned plenty of lines in the record books and could not be pleased with the way she gained another one.

She was truly embarrassed when she heard that Yegorova had admitted taking Bromantan, a substance which stirred controversy after several Russian athletes were caught using it at last year's Atlanta Olympics.
"It was a big shock and it was hard to find some sleep but we are top athletes and we did our best to win," said Vialbe after helping Russia to victory in Thursday's relay.
Before the start of that race, she had taken a microphone and apologised, saying the Russian team felt sorry but not responsible.

Yegorova said she had taken a Bromantan pill not knowing it was banned. She initially said she bore sole responsibility, although Russia's Tass news agency quoted her as saying she took it on the recommendation of her personal coach.

Viable, who was tested automatically after each race and was also selected four times for the new, pre-race blood tests aimed at detecting high haemoglobin levels, called the doping controls a good system that worked. "I always went to the tests knowing that I had nothing to fear," she added.
After again leaving her rivals helpless as she won the 30-km on Saturday, Vialbe jumped and screamed for joy, punching the air with clenched fists.
She bore a permanent smile during the press conference after her final victory, as if Yegorova's blunder were no longer on her mind.
"Now I'm going to celebrate," she said when there were no more questions, looking forward to a big party on the boat in the Trondheim harbour where the competitors are staying. "I deserve it."
